full_judgment: 3. The further facts necessary for disposal of the appeals are that in the year 1966 Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation Ltd. briefly PICIC, predecessor-in-interest of the BSRS, sanctioned to the Company M/s. Ashraf Jute Mills foreign currency loan for the establishment of a new Jute Mills at Kanchan, Narayanganj and subsequently sanctioned additional foreign currency loan and local currency loan and the Company utilized the foreign currency loan as well as local currency loan in selling up the said Mills; that the said Jute Mills was nationalized under PO 27 of 1972 and placed under the management and control of the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation from the 26th March, 1972; that in the year 1973 when the Jute Mills was under the management of the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation the BSRS sanctioned additional loan for completion of the expansion of the Mills and the aforesaid loan was sanctioned against the first mortgage/charge upon the assets and properties of the Company; that after the de-nationalization of the Jute Mills, the Company did not care to repay the loan taken from the BSRS and with a view to realizing the outstanding dues BSRS, pursuant to the instruction of the Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh, decided to sell the mortgaged properties of the borrower Company under Article 34 of PO 128 of 1972 read with BSRS Direct Sale of Mortgaged Properties Rules, 1981 and accordingly notice under Article 34 of the said Order was issued upon the Company and its Directors on 12.6.86; that on receipt of the reply from the Company the same was placed before the Managing Director of BSRS and the Managing Director of the BSRS asked the Company and its Directors to pay Tk. 4,970,700.00 which was due as on 1.1.86, that the, Company thereafter filed an application on 3.7.86 before the Board of Directors of BSRS which was not found acceptable by the Board of Directors of BSRS and accordingly the Board of Directors rejected the appeal of the Company and its Directors on 3.12.86; that BSRS then invited tender for sale of the assets and properties of the company under Article 34 of the BSRS Order and accordingly published sale notices in the Dainik Bangla and Bangladesh Times on 23.1.87 inviting tender on 14.2.87 but no tender was received in response to the said notices. Thereafter the borrower Company by their letter dated 23.5.87 informed the BSRS that the Rupali Bank Ltd. agreed to pay the debt of the borrower and prayed for maximum possible concession and in consideration thereof BSRS agreed to waive normal interest and penal interest and asked for payment of Tk. 4,02,49,398.00 as on 1.1.87 by June, 1987 but ultimately the Rupali Bank Ltd. informed the borrower Company with copy endorsed to BSRS that they were unable to assist the borrower Company; that in such circumstances BSRS with a view to realise the loan amount issued notice to the borrower and its directors on 8.10.87 informing them that it decided to initiate legal action under Article 35 of the BSRS Order and accordingly filed a certificate case to recover the loan amount of Tk. 6,21,87,779.11 as on 1.7.87 from the borrower Company; that thereafter the Managing Director of the Company by his letter dated 25.8.88 made a proposal to BSRS for transfer of their 51% shares to Mr. G L Modi of Uttara Jute Traders who was agreeable to make a down payment of 25% of the accrued interest and 25% of the principal loan amount; that due to this negotiation for transfer of shares BSRS kept in abeyance the proceedings under Articles 34 and 35 of the BSRS Order; that subsequently due to failure in reaching the negotiation with the Rupali Bank Ltd. regarding repayment of Bank's loan the said Mr. Modi by his letter dated 23.3.89 asked for refund of Tk. 1,34,27,687.00 which was already deposited by him in pursuance of the negotiation; that thereafter BSRS invited tender for the second time for direct sale of the assets and properties of the Company under Article 34 of the BSRS order by publishing notices in the Bangladesh Observer and the Daily Janata on 19.10.89 and 29.10.89 respectively inviting tender on 15.11.89, that with reference to this sale notice the Rupali Bank Ltd. by their letter dated 25.10.89 requested BSRS to assist the Bank in realising their dues amounting to Tk. 17,48,77,837.35 as on 31.12.88 from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged assets and properties of the borrower Company and in reply the BSRS by their letter dated 13.12.89 informed the Rupali Bank that if the assets and properties of the borrowers is sold at a price exceeding the dues of the BSRS then the question of distribution of the excess amount to other claimants would arise; that in pursuance of the said second sale notice only one tender was received which was not accepted by the Board of Directors of the BSRS; that thereafter tender notice for the 3rd time was published in the Daily Dainik Bangla and Bangladesh Times on 1.1.90 inviting tenders on 17.1.90 and in response to the notice three tenders were received and the offer of Tk. 6,04,65,000.00 by the Uttara Jute Fibres and Industries Ltd. being the highest, BSRS accepted that offer and accordingly issued the letter dated 1.3.90 asking the successful bidder to deposit the bid price; that the borrower company did not challenge this sale under Article 34 of the BSRS Order but before the possession of the mortgaged properties could be handed over to the purchaser the borrower-company moved the High Court Division of the Supreme Court by filing Writ Petition No. 807 of 1990 challenging the sale and transfer of the mortgaged assets and properties of the Company to the purchaser, Uttara Jute Fibres and Industries Ltd. and obtained an ad-interim order of stay on 25.4.90. Thereafter BSRS filed an application praying for vacating the order of stay before the Writ Bench and after hearing the parties the Writ Bench by the judgment and order dated 12.6.90 vacated the order of ad-interim stay granted on 25.4.90; that thereafter BSRS issued Sale Certificate to the buyers under Rule 10 of the BSRS (Direct Sale of Mortgaged Property) Rules, 1981; that the borrower-Company then filed Title Suit No. 328 of 1990 in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka and prayed therein for an injunction against the handing over of the mortgaged properties to the purchaser but the Court by an order dated 19.7.90 rejected the prayer of the borrower-Company; that in the meantime Rupali Bank Ltd. got the BSRS added as a party defendant in Money Suit No. 10 of 1980 filed by the Bank against the borrower-Company and its directors claiming a decree for an amount of Tk. 17,36,68,171.34 as on 1.1.89 on the allegation that the bank allowed over draft loan and cash credit to the borrower-Company against charge upon the raw jute, jute products and personal guarantee of the Directors of the Company and filed therein an application under Order 38 rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for attachment before judgment not only of the jute and jute goods and machinery parts claimed as charges but also of the land, building and machineries of the Mills; but the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka by his order dated 16.7.90 rejected the prayer of the Rupali Bank Ltd. for attachment of the land, building and machineries of the borrower- company which were sold by the BSRS to the Uttara Jute Fibres and Industries Ltd. and the Court directed the BSRS not to hand over the jute and jute goods to the purchaser as the Rupali Bank claimed first charge over the same; that thereafter on 21.7.90 BSRS handed over the possession of the mortgaged land, building and machineries of the borrower-company to the purchaser Uttara Jute Fibres and Industries Ltd.; that after taking possession of the assets and properties of the Jute Mills the purchaser asked the Rupaii Bank Ltd. to remove the jute and jute goods from the godown so that the purchaser may start their function in the Mills; that since in spite of several requests Rupali Bank did not remove the jute and jute goods from the Mills premises, the purchaser requested the BSRS to take necessary steps for removal of the jute and jute goods from the Mills premises and ultimately the purchaser by their letter dated 25.10.90 gave ultimatum to BSRS for taking immediate steps. But since the Rupaii Bank did not take any step to remove the jute and jute goods from the Mills premises and since this Court in Matter No.9 of 1987, in the meantime, has passed an order on 9.8.90 winding up the borrower-company, the BSRS prayed for a direction of the learned Company Judge upon the Rupali Bank Ltd. to remove the jute and jute goods from the Mills premises, by filing an affidavit of facts on 17.3.91.
